pr_title: SQL: Fix literal projection with condition
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/64567

Queries with a literal selection and a filter like `SELECT 1 FROM test_emp WHERE gender = 'F'` are currently erroneously optimised to use a local relation. This causes ES to always return a single record, no matter how many records match the filter condition.

This PR makes sure that `SkipQueryIfFoldingProjection` only skips the query if it's an aggregate with only constants (e.g. `SELECT 'foo' FROM test GROUP BY 1`). This optimization seems to lead to another issue https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/74064 that's not yet addressed in this PR.

Besides this the "skip query" optimization, the `SkipQueryIfFoldingProjection` class also folds constants from `LocalRelation`s and pushes the evaluated values into a new `LocalRelation` (e.g. for queries like `SELECT 1 + 2`).
pr_comments:
I've addressed your comments and also tried to consolidate the partially duplicated logic of the `Project` and `Aggregate` cases. Thanks to the consolidated logic and the `collectFirstDown` method it should also use less traversals through the query tree.

Please have another look.

@costin please have another look, I've addressed your comments and the implementation should now also be more robust against some cases where the optimization might have erroneously be applied when it shouldn't. E.g. there might be cases (in the future?) with more than one Project/Aggregate or Relation.

I'm hesitant of introducing `Relation` as I'm not sure it adds much value in general and even in this case I'm only interested in two specific relations and not e.g. `UnresolvedRelation` or the EQL `LocalRelation`. The `collectLeaves` approach seems sufficient to me.

issue_context.title: SQL: wrong result on literal selection with condition
issue_context.body:
While 
`SELECT * FROM test_emp WHERE languages = 0` correctly returns nothing (there's no match for the filter), 
`SELECT true FROM test_emp WHERE languages = 0` wrongly returns one row/column result: `true`.  Noteworthy, 
`SELECT true FROM test_emp WHERE false` returns nothing, es expected.
comments:
I've found a related inconsistency when using literal selection:

`SELECT gender, 1 FROM test_emp WHERE gender = 'F'` retrieves 

```
    gender     |       1       
---------------+---------------
F              |1              
F              |1              
F              |1              
...
```

and `SELECT 1 FROM test_emp` retrieves

```
       1       
---------------
1              
1              
1   
...
```

but `SELECT 1 FROM test_emp WHERE gender = 'F'` only retrieves a single record like `SELECT 1` would:

```
       1       
---------------
1              
```

I think the expected behaviour is to retrieve a `1` for every document matching the condition.
Yep, that's correct it should return as many rows as if a field from a table was selected, so the last one with the filter `WHERE gender = 'F'` is incorrect behaviour.

review_comments:
The if/else could be optimized by swapping it around and avoid checking for Project:
```
if (projectOrAggregate instanceof Aggregate) {
 ...
 }
else if (isNonSkippedLocalRelation) // no need to check for Project
```
